description: Generalist software engineer building robust backend services, data structures, APIs, and scalable distributed architectures.
default_interviewer_tone: Direct, technical, tech-lead caliber; probes for architectural trade-offs; warm but concise.

question_style_notes.entry: Verbal problem-solving prompts (e.g. streaming data, choosing hash maps vs trees) and coursework/project architecture. No assumption of enterprise production scale.
question_style_notes.mid: Production trade-offs, API versioning, error boundaries, concurrency bugs, and service boundaries.
question_style_notes.senior: Distributed failure modes, database indexing and isolation, cross-service consensus, and operational latency profiling.
question_style_notes.lead: System architecture evolution, SLA vs infrastructure cost balance, engineering standards, and technical incident governance.

skills.name: Data Structures & Problem Solving
skills.description: Selects, analyzes, and implements optimal data structures and algorithmic complexity bounds for high-throughput computational workloads.
skills.rubric_l1: Fails basic algorithmic analysis; defaults to O(N^2) brute-force without recognizing hash table or two-pointer simplifications.
skills.rubric_l2: Selects standard collections (arrays, hash maps) correctly but struggles with space-time trade-offs and edge cases like overflow or off-by-one bounds.
skills.rubric_l3: Designs clean, production-grade algorithms with verified optimal time and auxiliary space complexity, handling corner cases cleanly.
skills.rubric_l4: Optimizes algorithmic trade-offs, amortized complexity, bounded memory collections, and high-throughput data processing under heavy load.
skills.rubric_l5: Applies lock-free algorithmic primitives, customized memory allocators, or hardware-aware bitwise structures for ultra-low latency.

L2: Identifies baseline time and auxiliary space complexity for standard array and map operations.
Selects appropriate built-in data structures (lists, hash sets, queues) to solve standard algorithmic tasks.
Verifies boundary conditions such as empty collections, single-item inputs, and index boundaries.
L3: Implements optimal algorithmic solutions meeting strict O(N) or O(N log N) runtime bounds.
Evaluates auxiliary memory overhead and avoids unnecessary object allocations during hot-path execution.
Analyzes amortized runtime behavior for dynamic data structures under continuous mutation.
L4: Restructures algorithmic data access patterns to minimize amortized complexity and auxiliary allocation overhead under heavy load.
Identifies and eliminates hidden non-linear complexity bottlenecks in core operational loops.
Designs thread-safe collections utilizing read-write locks or fine-grained concurrency control.
L5: Architects lock-free or wait-free algorithmic primitives using atomic operations to prevent thread contention.
Evaluates algorithmic trade-offs against underlying memory bus bandwidth and cache hierarchy constraints.

question_patterns.entry_prompt: Suppose you are receiving a continuous stream of numeric events and need to return the top K most frequent items at any moment; talk me through the data structures and complexity trade-offs you would consider.
question_patterns.mid_prompt: Walk me through how you diagnosed and resolved an unexpected algorithmic bottleneck in a service whose processing latency degraded as payload volume scaled.
question_patterns.senior_prompt: Walk me through how you redesigned a data structure hot path to eliminate memory allocation churn and maximize cache line throughput under peak write load.

skills.name: Core CS Fundamentals
skills.description: Applies operating system concepts, concurrency primitives, thread lifecycles, network sockets, and memory models.
skills.rubric_l1: Lacks clarity on processes vs threads; confuses stack vs heap memory and socket protocols.
skills.rubric_l2: Understands processes vs threads but cannot diagnose race conditions, deadlocks, or socket connection limits.
skills.rubric_l3: Correctly employs synchronization primitives (mutexes, semaphores, channels) and explains TCP/UDP connection handshakes.
skills.rubric_l4: Diagnoses race conditions, thread starvation, socket exhaustion (TIME_WAIT), and kernel vs user-space context switching overhead.
skills.rubric_l5: Architects high-performance non-blocking I/O event loops and reasons about CPU memory barriers and instruction reordering.

L2: Differentiates between stack and heap memory allocation lifecycles.
Explains the operational differences between process memory isolation and shared thread memory.
Identifies common socket communication states and HTTP protocol layers.
L3: Applies mutexes, semaphores, or channels to safeguard shared state across concurrent execution threads.
Traces network request lifecycles from DNS lookup through TCP 3-way handshake to socket read.
Prevents common deadlock conditions by establishing consistent lock acquisition ordering.
L4: Diagnoses subtle race conditions and memory leaks using profiling tools and thread dumps.
Mitigates OS-level resource limits including file descriptor limits and socket TIME_WAIT exhaustion.
Explains context switching latency and CPU core affinity trade-offs in multithreaded runtimes.
L5: Designs asynchronous non-blocking event loops using epoll/kqueue models for massive socket concurrency.
Analyzes CPU memory visibility models, cache coherence protocols (MESI), and memory barriers.

question_patterns.entry_prompt: Suppose two worker threads need to process and increment items in a shared counter queue; talk me through how you ensure data consistency without corrupting memory.
question_patterns.mid_prompt: Walk me through a time you tracked down a tricky multithreading race condition or memory leak in a backend service.
question_patterns.senior_prompt: Walk me through how you designed a high-concurrency connection handler to prevent thread pool exhaustion and kernel context switching overhead.

skills.name: Backend & API Design
skills.description: Designs robust REST/gRPC interfaces, idempotent write semantics, authentication boundaries, and input validation schemas.
skills.rubric_l1: Creates inconsistent endpoint schemas, neglects HTTP status codes, and ignores error response bodies.
skills.rubric_l2: Implements basic CRUD endpoints with standard HTTP verbs but lacks pagination, idempotency, or contract versioning.
skills.rubric_l3: Produces clean RESTful or gRPC APIs with cursor-based pagination, consistent error contracts, and secure request validation.
skills.rubric_l4: Designs robust idempotent payment/mutation semantics using deduplication keys, backward-compatible schemas, and rate limiting.
skills.rubric_l5: Designs resilient cross-service API contracts, zero-trust authentication boundaries, and automated schema evolution across microservices.

L2: Follows REST conventions for HTTP methods, path parameter naming, and appropriate status codes.
Implements input validation to reject malformed or missing payload attributes.
Applies basic offset-based pagination and standard JSON response envelopes.
L3: Designs robust cursor-based pagination for high-volume collections to prevent database offset degradation.
Implements idempotency key verification on mutation endpoints to guarantee safe retry behavior.
Structures uniform API error contracts providing actionable error codes without leaking internal stack traces.
L4: Architects distributed rate limiting using token bucket or sliding window algorithms across edge gateways.
Maintains backward and forward schema compatibility across multiple concurrently active API versions.
Defines granular authentication and role-based authorization boundaries at the API gateway layer.
L5: Engineers service-level zero-trust authentication boundaries and mutual TLS communication between backend services.
Designs backward-compatible schema evolution strategies and automated contract testing pipelines across service boundaries.

question_patterns.entry_prompt: Suppose you are designing an API endpoint that returns a user's notification feed; talk me through how you would structure the request parameters, pagination, and error responses.
question_patterns.mid_prompt: Walk me through how you designed an API endpoint that handles financial transactions or inventory updates to guarantee safe retries without duplicate executions.
question_patterns.senior_prompt: Walk me through how you managed a major breaking change in a widely used external API while maintaining zero downtime and backward compatibility.

skills.name: System Design & Scalability
skills.description: Architects distributed systems utilizing caching layers, message queues, database sharding, and resilience mechanisms.
skills.rubric_l1: Proposes single-server monoliths; ignores caching, replication, and single points of failure.
skills.rubric_l2: Mentions Redis and load balancers generically but cannot explain cache invalidation, write policies, or replication lag.
skills.rubric_l3: Designs reliable distributed topologies incorporating reverse proxies, read-replicas, asynchronous queues, and cache strategies.
skills.rubric_l4: Incorporates circuit breakers, bulkhead isolation, distributed consensus, and idempotent event consumers under network partitions.
skills.rubric_l5: Evaluates storage engine trade-offs (LSM vs B-Tree), global active-active quorum, and balances infrastructure cost against SLAs.

L2: Explains the function of reverse proxies, load balancers, and horizontal scaling in backend systems.
Identifies single points of failure in basic single-node database and application topologies.
Distinguishes between synchronous HTTP calls and asynchronous message queue delivery.
L3: Designs resilient multi-tier architectures with read replicas, caching layers, and asynchronous background workers.
Formulates cache invalidation and write-through/cache-aside strategies preventing stale reads.
Applies message queues (RabbitMQ/Kafka) to decouple high-load ingestion from slow processing pipelines.
L4: Implements circuit breakers, retries with exponential backoff and jitter, and backpressure mechanisms.
Designs database sharding strategies and evaluates rebalancing overhead across partition keys.
Guarantees message processing semantics (at-least-once with idempotent consumer deduplication).
L5: Architects multi-region active-active distributed databases with conflict resolution and tunable quorum consistency.
Evaluates storage engine trade-offs (LSM trees vs B+ trees) based on read-to-write ratio and write amplification.

question_patterns.entry_prompt: Suppose an application needs to store and quickly display user profile pictures; talk me through the architectural components you would use from the browser to cloud storage.
question_patterns.mid_prompt: Walk me through how you designed a system that experienced a 10x traffic spike while keeping downstream database latencies within acceptable bounds.
question_patterns.senior_prompt: Walk me through how you architected a mission-critical distributed service to survive partial datacenter outages without dropping in-flight client writes.

skills.name: Debugging & Testing
skills.description: Diagnoses production incidents, interprets telemetry logs and stack traces, and enforces automated testing strategies.
skills.rubric_l1: Relies entirely on print statements; cannot interpret stack traces or write automated test cases.
skills.rubric_l2: Writes standard unit tests with mocks but struggles with integration test boundaries and diagnosing intermittent flake.
skills.rubric_l3: Constructs comprehensive unit and integration test suites; systematically isolates production bugs using APM and logs.
skills.rubric_l4: Profiles CPU/memory flame graphs to isolate production stalls; creates hermetic integration test environments and chaos experiments.
skills.rubric_l5: Drives post-mortem root cause analysis culture; builds automated canary rollback pipelines and continuous verification frameworks.

L2: Writes unit tests verifying standard happy-path inputs and common error conditions.
Interprets stack traces to isolate the originating source file and failing line of code.
Uses debugger breakpoints and structured logging statements to trace variable mutation.
L3: Constructs integration tests using test containers or ephemeral databases to verify service boundaries.
Systematically debugs production errors using centralized logs, correlation IDs, and APM metrics.
Identifies and eliminates non-deterministic flaky tests in CI pipelines.
L4: Analyzes memory heaps and CPU flame graphs to identify memory leaks and thread lock contention.
Simulates network latency and dependency failure modes using chaos engineering techniques.
Designs contract tests verifying upstream and downstream API schema compatibility.
L5: Leads complex blameless post-mortem investigations and establishes preventative architectural guardrails.
Architects automated canary deployment gates that trigger immediate rollbacks on anomalous error budget burn.

question_patterns.entry_prompt: Suppose a unit test passes locally on your laptop but fails intermittently on the CI server; talk me through how you would investigate and isolate the issue.
question_patterns.mid_prompt: Walk me through how you investigated a severe production latency spike where the root cause was not immediately apparent from error logs.
question_patterns.senior_prompt: Walk me through how you established automated testing and release guardrails to prevent regressions in a system with legacy dependencies.

skills.name: Project & Experience Deep-Dive
skills.description: Structured walkthrough of the candidate's own projects and work: scope, ownership, architecture decisions, trade-offs, and outcomes. Follow-ups probe what the candidate actually said they built.
skills.rubric_l1: Cannot describe any project coherently; vague about own role, stack, or outcome; claims work without substance.
skills.rubric_l2: Describes a project at surface level; can name the stack and own tasks but struggles with design decisions, trade-offs, or measurable outcomes.
skills.rubric_l3: Clearly explains a real project: goal, architecture, own ownership, technologies used, and key trade-offs with reasons; can dive one level deeper on any part when probed.
skills.rubric_l4: Deep command of own work: quantified outcomes, alternatives considered, failure modes handled, and how constraints shaped the design; connects project decisions to broader engineering principles.
skills.rubric_l5: Exceptional narrative and reflection: articulates the business/technical context, led non-trivial trade-offs, mentors others through the reasoning, and honestly separates team work from individual contribution.

l2: Names the project goal, stack, and their own tasks.
l3: Explains the architecture and their specific ownership area.
Justifies key design or technology choices with trade-offs.
l4: Quantifies outcomes or impact (performance, scale, users, grades of improvement).
Handles a follow-up on any component they described without hand-waving.
l5: Reflects on what they would change with hindsight and why.

question_patterns.anchor: Walk me through the most significant project you have built or contributed to — what it does, your role, and the stack you chose.
question_patterns.anchor_alt: Pick any project, class assignment, or hackathon you enjoyed — what did you build and what did you personally work on?
question_patterns.escalation: If that project had to serve 10x the users or data tomorrow, what would break first and what would you change?
probes: Why did you choose that stack over the alternatives you considered?
What was the hardest bug or setback in that project, and how did you resolve it?
Which part are you proudest of, and which part would you rebuild differently now?
How did you verify it actually worked — tests, metrics, or user feedback?
